durable.evidence: Items are files flushed to disk before they are renamed into place, and the head is read back from their names; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 reads on from a cursor, and puts the next seq, from a fresh runspace that shares no state with the writer.

realtime.evidence: A watch polls the mailbox's names every 50 ms; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 has another runspace put while a watch waits, and requires the watch to return within a second of that put.

reach.remote.evidence: Mailboxes are folders on this machine's disk; no other machine reaches them. A channel between machines requires reach.remote, so it never picks this relay.

trim.on.ack.evidence: An ack writes a floor marker and deletes the items through it; test/test-relay-conformance.ps1 reads only what is after the ack and sees the next put numbered after the trimmed ones.
